title: NRC Update Call on Report 1398274, PHMSA Bridged In

fields.orgName: Ironbark Pipeline Company, Pipeline Control Center, Tulsa

caller.name: NRC Duty Officer Reyes, with PHMSA Central Region Inspector Hollis bridged in
caller.label: National Response Center

callee.name: Nadia Kowalczyk
callee.label: Control Center Shift Supervisor, Prairie Line

transcript.speaker: NRC
transcript.text: Ironbark Pipeline Control Center, this is the National Response Center calling back on report one-three-nine-eight-two-seven-four. Am I speaking with the person in charge for the Prairie Line?

transcript.speaker: CCSS
transcript.text: Confirm who you are and give your call-back number.

transcript.speaker: NRC
transcript.text: Thank you. I'm calling to take your update on 1398274. I also have the PHMSA Central Region inspector on the line. He asked me to bridge him in so he hears the same numbers you give me. Inspector, go ahead.

transcript.speaker: PHMSA
transcript.text: Morning again. This is Hollis, PHMSA Office of Pipeline Safety, Central Region. We spoke at nine-fifteen. I'll stay quiet while the NRC takes your update. After that I have three things to put on the record.

transcript.speaker: NRC
transcript.text: Okay. Your original report shows two thousand seven hundred to three thousand five hundred barrels of medium sour crude, Prairie Line, milepost 214.3, Kansas River crossing, line shut in at 06:04. What's your current quantity, and what's it based on?

transcript.speaker: CCSS
transcript.text: Give the updated release quantity, its basis, and whether it is confirmed.

transcript.speaker: NRC
transcript.text: Got it. And did any of the recovered oily water go into that number, or is that tracked separately? The EPA Region 7 duty officer asked me to check.

transcript.speaker: CCSS
transcript.text: Answer the question about the recovered liquid.

transcript.speaker: NRC
transcript.text: Okay. The cause field still says 'unknown.' I've had two calls this morning from media saying it was corrosion, and somebody mentioned an excavator. Do you want to change the cause field?

transcript.speaker: CCSS
transcript.text: State what goes in the cause field.

transcript.speaker: NRC
transcript.text: Understood, I'll leave it as entered. I'll pass this update to EPA Region 7, KDHE and PHMSA as usual. Inspector, it's yours.

transcript.speaker: PHMSA
transcript.text: Thanks. First, I need the forty-eight-hour update to the NRC on 1398274 with the revised volume. It sounds like you've just given that, so make sure your written records show the same number and basis. Second, I'm formally requesting your control-room records: the full alarm and event history for the Prairie Bend segment from 05:50 yesterday on, the close times for Mill Ridge and Sandhill, the CPM and volume-balance runs, and your notification call log. Please keep the originals. Don't overwrite, purge or edit them.

transcript.speaker: PHMSA
transcript.text: About that call log: when I get the final version I want each notification with the time, the person spoken to and what was said. For the two water systems, which times will be on it?

transcript.speaker: CCSS
transcript.text: Tell PHMSA which notification times the final log will show for the water systems, and confirm the records will be kept.

transcript.speaker: PHMSA
transcript.text: Third, I'm requesting that you hold off on any excavation, cutting or repair at the crossing until we've talked about preserving the failed section for metallurgical analysis. I'm not stopping your spill response on the river. This is about the pipe itself. Who's my point of contact at the command post, and do you have anything on cause?

transcript.speaker: CCSS
transcript.text: Name a point of contact and answer the question on cause.

transcript.speaker: PHMSA
transcript.text: Fair enough. I'll put the records request in writing to your QI within the hour. Thanks, both of you.

voiceStyles.NRC: Woman in her 30s, calm and procedural. She reads back numbers carefully, with keyboard typing in a quiet operations room behind her.
voiceStyles.PHMSA: Man in his 50s, measured and formal, an experienced regulator. Courteous but precise, and slows down on the records request. Sounds like he's on a cell phone in a vehicle.

instructorNote: This tests whether the CCSS gives the NRC the VB-0621 range (2,900–3,300 bbl, metered imbalance plus surveyed drain-down, estimate, not confirmed), keeps the recovered oily liquid separate and leaves the cause as unknown, and whether the team keeps the alarm, valve and call records for PHMSA. The final log should show each utility as notified only when its operator was reached, not at the clerk and voicemail times. Once the call ends, say aloud that IC Gordon Iwata wants a one-page after-action note before the 09:45 Unified Command briefing, and watch that the PIO brings the JIC figure in line with the NRC update.
